title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on the Implementation of the Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards to Which China Has Acceded

articles.content_en:
1. In accordance with the reciprocity reservation declaration made by China upon acceding to the Convention, China shall apply the Convention to the recognition and enforcement of arbitral awards made in the territory of another Contracting State. Where the Convention has different provisions from China's Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), the provisions of the Convention shall prevail.
For arbitral awards made in the territory of a non-Contracting State that require recognition and enforcement by Chinese courts, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation).

2. In accordance with the commercial reservation declaration made by China upon acceding to the Convention, China shall apply the Convention only to disputes arising from contractual and non-contractual commercial legal relationships under Chinese law. The so-called "contractual and non-contractual commercial legal relationships" specifically refer to economic rights and obligations arising from contracts, torts, or in accordance with relevant legal provisions, such as sales of goods, property leases, engineering contracts, processing and subcontracting, technology transfer, joint ventures, cooperative ventures, exploration and development of natural resources, insurance, credit, labor services, agency, consulting services, and passenger and freight transportation by sea, civil aviation, railway, and road, as well as product liability, environmental pollution, maritime accidents, and ownership disputes, but shall not include disputes between foreign investors and host governments.

4. Upon receiving an application from a party, the people's court of China with jurisdiction shall review the arbitral award for which recognition and enforcement are sought. If it considers that none of the circumstances listed in Article V(1) and (2) of the 1958 New York Convention exist, it shall rule to recognize the validity of the award and enforce it in accordance with the procedures provided in the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation). If it determines that any of the circumstances listed in Article V(2) exists, or if it is proved, based on evidence provided by the party against whom enforcement is sought, that any of the circumstances listed in Article V(1) exists, it shall rule to dismiss the application and refuse recognition and enforcement.

5. The arbitral awards for which recognition and enforcement are sought with Chinese courts shall be limited to those made in the territory of another Contracting State after the 1958 New York Convention took effect with respect to China. Such application shall be submitted within the time limit for applying for enforcement as provided in Article 169 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation).
